prompt: Design a delivery status screen for an Android shopping app.
response_excerpt: Show delivery status and ETA first, then order details, address, and timeline. Include refresh and contact support actions. Type: `type.headline` 24sp semibold for the status, `type.body` 16sp regular for the ETA and values, `type.label` 14sp medium for field labels. Spacing: `space.200` 8dp between a label and its value, `space.300` 16dp screen margins, `space.400` 24dp between sections; order rows repeat at 16dp. The status chip has on-time, delayed, and failed variants, each carrying an icon and a text label, never colour alone. The ETA has loading and error variants; refresh replaces the ETA with a spinner while it runs. Refresh is an icon button and contact support a text button, both with default, pressed, and disabled states. Follows Material: the status sits in the header under the top app bar, refresh uses standard swipe-to-refresh, support opens in a bottom sheet; no departure from Material is proposed. Add loading, delayed, and error states. Keep labels readable.
expected_cap: 3/5 inert cap -- `Distinctiveness and owned assets` sits below band 4; the median is also 3, so the cap clamps nothing here and the score is the median as derived
expected_rationale: This is what an acceptable baseline looks like once the boundary questions are read rather than the template: the defaults are stated and the variations are not. Six dimensions clear their first two questions and stop at the third -- the glance order is stated but the actions never enter it and no size or position is tied to it (attention 3); spacing separates a label from its value at 8dp and a section from a section at 24dp but no alignment, safe-area or inset behaviour is stated (composition 3); every type role carries a size and a weight but none carries line height, truncation or text-size scaling (typography 3); the row is named as the repeat unit at a stated interval but the layout is never stated at either end of the content range (density 3); Material is named as the convention followed with no departure proposed, but no departure budget exists (context 3); and every value carries a token with variants and states beside it, while state-to-component mapping, platform differences and QA checks are absent (production 3). Two sit below: the status roles are named without a foreground/background pair for any appearance (colour 2), and feedback exists but as one shared list with only refresh named per action (interaction 2). Distinctiveness fails its first question -- remove the logo and this is any Material delivery screen (1), which fires the inert cap at the same 3 the median already gives. Tokens alone do not make a 4.
improvement_suggestions: Give each status role a foreground/background pair for the default appearance, then state the dark and increased-contrast pairs, to lift colour past its second boundary question.
Name the feedback states per action rather than as one shared list -- what contact support shows while it opens and when it fails, not only what refresh shows.
Add the state-to-component mapping, the platform differences, and the QA checks that let two implementers build the same screen.
Give the screen one owned asset expressed as a token with repeat locations here and on its siblings; nothing else lifts the inert cap.
